criteria.notes: Corpus composition at HEAD: 33 fixtures — 25 `attack-*` (every one carrying `expectedStages`) and 8 `valid-*`, one per `ArtifactKind`. All eight vectors the criterion names are present, several more than once: bidi (attack-bidi-override), zero-width (attack-zero-width, plus attack-lrm-rlm-direction-marks and attack-line-paragraph-separator), confusable (attack-confusable-domain, attack-confusable-greek-alpha), secret/credential (8 fixtures: aws, pem, connection-string, anthropic, openai-project, gcp, github-fine-grained-pat, raw-jwt), remote image (attack-remote-image), HTML/script/data-URL (attack-html-injection, attack-html-injection-slash-attribute, attack-script-url, attack-data-url, attack-adf-link-javascript-href), attribution/engine-name (attack-attribution-leak, attack-engine-name-leak), over-length (attack-over-length), unevidenced claim (attack-unevidenced-claim, attack-unevidenced-claim-standard-token). Two honest scope statements. (a) RED-THEN-GREEN PROVENANCE. Unlike phases 01-05/07, phase 17 committed no `wiN-*-failing.txt` transcripts, so the ORIGINAL red-then-green is evidenced only by the phase README's own remediation record quoted above, not by a captured failing run from the build. What the closeout adds is a different and weaker-scoped thing, and is labelled as such: closeout-c1b is a mutation probe run TODAY proving the corpus suite is a real gate capable of failing, not a reconstruction of the 2026-07 red. The substantive guarantee the box carries — every attack fixture in the directory is blocked — is fully evidenced by the CI run, the universal-quantifier assertion and the local re-run. (b) SCOPE OF "secret/credential leak", stated so the tick is not read wider than it is: `docs/evidence/phase-17/README.md` §Documented deviations 12 records that `SECRET_PATTERNS` is 'a fixed, curated list, expanded but not made exhaustive'. This is 17's OWN pattern set; roadmap/17 §Out of scope states that 14's source-diff secret scanning and this stage 'are maintained independently, with no dependency edge between 14 and 17', so nothing in phase 14's coverage backs this box and nothing in this box backs 14's. (c) Stale-evidence flag, not a defect in the criterion: `docs/evidence/phase-17/README.md`'s exit-criterion-1 mapping row still says the corpus holds '22 fixtures: 14 attack + 8 valid' and lists 14 attack files — a pre-remediation count contradicted by the same README's own section above it ('Corpus grew from 22 to 33 fixtures'). At HEAD it is 33/25/8. Left unedited per the pass rule against fixing findings in the same pass.

criteria.notes: Closed by remediation, not by re-reading the old bearer. The previous bearer (the it() whose name matched this criterion) asserted six toContain() calls over a hand-written markdown string and never loaded a fixture or called lint(); it is replaced, not reinterpreted. Writing the real assertion made the box RED and surfaced two production defects, both fixed in the same change: (1) url-policy knew only the markdown image notation ![alt](url), so an embedded remote image written in Jira WIKI-MARKUP notation — !https://evil.example/x.png!, the format phase 19 actually puts on the wire for Data Center — linted clean; (2) toWikiMarkup rewrote ![alt](url) into ![alt|url], a stray '!' glued to a link, which handed url-policy a construct it permits and so converted a BLOCKED artifact into a CLEAN one. toWikiMarkup now emits Jira image syntax !url! and url-policy recognizes both notations. Mutation evidence, each arm rebuilt first because connectors-jira imports @crabgic/renderer from dist (baseline 68 files / 793 tests): making WIKI_IMAGE_PATTERN unmatchable gives 5 failed / 788 passed; making the image pass an identity gives 2 failed / 791 passed; restore returns 793. The cited CI run executed commit 5c0a8f8, this branch's code commit. criteria.notes: Two limits of the check, stated so the tick is not read as more than it is. (a) It is a NAME-substring denylist over this package's own manifest; it cannot see a transitive HTTP client. That hole is closed here by inspection rather than by the test — `@crabgic/contracts` is the only runtime dependency and it pulls only `zod`/`zod-to-json-schema` — and the inspection is recorded above rather than left implicit. (b) It is a manifest check, not a call-graph check: it proves no HTTP/VCS SDK is DECLARED, which is exactly what the criterion's words ask ('a static manifest check … structurally, not just by test absence'), and it does not by itself prove the package makes no `node:https` call. Stale-evidence flag, not a defect: `docs/evidence/phase-17/README.md`'s exit-criterion-7 row still quotes the manifest as `dependencies: { "@eo/contracts": "0.0.0" }` — a pre-rename artifact from the original build; at HEAD it is `@crabgic/contracts`, and the test asserts the current name.
